children: , the cloud and enterprise-software giant, committed to ten enforceable AI safeguards through an agreement with two major teachers unions. The stock edged approximately 0.1% higher to $492.41 Thursday.

The rules draw sharp boundaries around AI in classrooms. Microsoft cannot train models on student or educator data, must limit data collection and provide plain-language disclosures, while AI companions are prohibited and high-risk decisions require human oversight. Starting in November, school districts can add these protections to new or existing Microsoft contracts without reopening the entire agreement.

The immediate revenue impact remains unclear because Microsoft does not separately report education sales. Still, the strategic logic is clear: tighter privacy commitments could preserve access to schools after New York City and Los Angeles placed one-year restrictions on many student-facing AI tools. Microsoft Cloud produced $59.3 billion in revenue last quarter as companywide capital spending reached $41 billion. The picture adds a valuation angle, showing Microsoft trading 15.59% below its GF Value estimate of $583.36a sizable gap if stronger trust helps defend its education footprint.

title: Microsoft's New School AI Rules Sacrifice Data to Preserve Access
